1#א: ["Forbidden in benefit, etc. It is explained in the Gemara in Avodah Zarah (daf 74a) that prohibitions of benefit — such as basar b'chalav and the like — if they are a piece worthy of honor, forbid their mixture also from benefit even in a thousand; and so is it among the poskim. And see Ran there. And see siman 109 s.k. 5. However, it is permitted to sell them to a non Jew except for the value of the prohibition within them, as I wrote below siman 110 s.k. 2:"]
1#ב: ["And if it is a doubt whether it is a piece worthy of honor, etc. For a piece worthy of honor that is not nullified in the majority is d'rabbanan, and a d'rabbanan doubt is decided leniently — and this is specifically a doubt whether it is a piece worthy of honor; but if it is certainly a piece worthy of honor and the prohibition is doubtful, it is not nullified, as below siman 110 seif 9 — see there:"]
2#א: ["And basar b'chalav. For since each one is permitted on its own, and through their joining together they became forbidden, the whole reverted to being as one body:"]
2#ב: ["It does not have the status of a piece worthy of honor. The reason is as the Hagahot ShaDa wrote in siman 41, and Rashba, Ran, and other poskim — because from the place of absorption the prohibition absorbed in it is not considered significant."]
2#ג: ["And even a piece that was not salted, etc. See above siman 99 seif 14 and what is written there:"]
2#ד: ["Every piece that was forbidden only on account of a peel, etc. It is written in Sefer Lev Chaim (daf 210b): and it requires study — from where was it forbidden on account of a peel? Only because it absorbed taste from another prohibition; and if so, even when the whole piece became forbidden, etc. end of his words. And to reconcile this: for we find it in basar b'chalav, etc. — investigate. In any case, what the Rav brought from Tosafot was not found; only that Tosafot at the beginning of the chapter of Gid HaNasheh (Chullin daf 96) wrote regarding a place of cutting, etc. — see there. And what the Shach wrote in the name of Lev Chaim is puzzling, for the peel itself has no prohibition upon it, etc. — investigate. And it appears that he holds that even if it is not rendered nevelah, nevertheless if it is possible to squeeze it out it is forbidden, as below siman 106, etc. — see there. And Tosafot in several places in Chullin and in the passage "a piece that absorbed," etc., hold that this depends on one another — it is impossible for the piece to become nevelah if it is possible to squeeze it out it is forbidden; we do not say thus; since the peel did not become nevelah, if it is possible to squeeze it out it is permitted and there is no prohibition upon it, and tomorrow it will return to being permitted — how can we say it is a piece worthy of honor? This is one point. Furthermore, since we hold like Rabbeinu Tam that a peel does not forbid its mixture in wet-with-wet, and one does not even need sixty, even though the taste is d'oraisa — how can we say that in dry-with-dry they will not be nullified on account of a peel, even in a thousand, on account of a piece worthy of honor, which is entirely a rabbinic decree? For regarding nosen taam d'oraisa we are not concerned, and for a rabbinic matter we are concerned — this matter has no relevance. And Rabeinu Yerucham and the other poskim who hold that a peel has the status of a piece worthy of honor hold thus because they hold like Riva that wet-with-wet forbids with nosen taam and requires sixty — and so too in dry. But we, who hold like Rabbeinu Tam that one does not need sixty against the peel and it does not forbid the mixture at all, it is obvious that we do not apply a piece worthy of honor to it. And the Rama ruled well:"]
3#א: ["A chicken in its feathers, etc. — it is nullified, etc. It is implied from the words of the Mechaber and the poskim that even a counted item (davar sheb'minyan) is not so — and as Maharshal wrote in his rulings and in his book Piskei HaGahot siman 53, that when it lacks a very great preparation it is also not a counted item; and this is clearly implied in Mordechai at the beginning of Beitzah — see there. And so is the opinion of the Bach, unlike the Torat Chatat who wrote in general rule 43 that even though it was nullified on account of being worthy of honor, it was not nullified on account of being a counted item — see above:"]
3#ב: ["And even though after it was mixed they removed the feathers. Nevertheless, since at the beginning of the mixture it was nullified, it does not revert to being prohibited when stirred. Sefer Mitzvot Katan:"]
3#ג: ["And likewise a whole sheep. Even if its skin was removed:"]
3#ד: ["Except for a chicken in its feathers. And a sheep in its skin, and the like:"]
3#ה: ["Except for goose feet. And the Torat Chatat wrote there in the name of Maharai that goose legs whose skin was not singed off them as people are accustomed to do are comparable to a chicken in its feathers:"]
4#א: ["Fat of the stomach lining, etc. And in Piskei Tosafot on Nedarim siman 80 I found that they wrote: and it requires study regarding the outer membrane of the stomach with its fat — perhaps it is worthy of honor — end of his words. And it appears that everything depends on time and place:"]
4#ב: ["But the skin of goose fat, etc. And Maharshal disagrees with this; and since these laws vary according to place and time, as the Rambam and poskim wrote, and as below at the beginning of siman 110, I have been brief in this, and everything depends on the judgment of the teacher whether it is considered worthy of honor in that place — if not, it is nullified; and if there is doubt, we are lenient, as above seif 1 in the hagahah:"]
5#_: Gizzard, etc. It is implied from the language of the Mechaber that even the gizzard of a goose is included; and so is implied from the words of other poskim. But Maharshal wrote in his rulings and in his book Piskei HaGahot siman 50 that a gizzard is not nullified; and so is found in the name of Maharam in the hagahah below beginning "Maharam forbade a needle found in a gizzard," etc., that he ruled thus — end of his words (and after him the Bach followed). And incidentally he did not examine well, for one who examines there in siman 54 in that hagahah will see that Maharam's ruling applies specifically to a piece that absorbed a prohibition and there is not sixty in it to nullify it, etc. — see there at length.
6#א: ["Or they were crushed. And the Torat Chatat wrote in general rule 40 at the end: and it is implied in Or Zarua that the ruling that it is nullified if crushed means that no significant item remained there; but if a piece worthy of honor remained, even though it is nullified on account of beriah, nevertheless it is still considered significant and is not nullified on account of a piece worthy of honor — and this is sound reasoning, end of his words. And see further in Beit Yosef and Torat Chatat what they wrote in the name of Maharai:"]
6#ב: ["And even after, etc. See above siman 99 s.k. (9) [15] and siman 110 s.k. 39:"]
6#ג: ["And that they were crushed without intent, etc. See above siman 99 seif 5 and what is written there:"]
6#ד: ["And there is no distinction whether they were mixed in their kind, etc. Meaning that a piece worthy of honor, even when not in its kind, is not nullified even in a thousand — unlike Or Zarua who wrote that a piece worthy of honor is nullified only in its kind. And see above siman 102 s.k. 4. And see below siman 109 s.k. 8 — I wrote there how we find a piece worthy of honor mixed not in its kind. And see siman 110 s.k. 1:"]
